why_this_repository: fred-data's README says FLoRA processing and data corrections belong in flora-validation; output/flora.csv on main is synced from its release.
identity: Corrections key on the permanent published id (flora_data.id, the FLORA-###### value in flora.csv). Row positions and full-record hashes are not identities.

reproduction_axis.note: The combined outcome, quote and source are derived from the axes, so only the changed axis is sent.

original_reference.note: A corrected doi_o re-joins metadata in the build. Dry-run the result against the authoritative record.

type_and_outcome.note: type is not an editable field in flora_edits.FIELD_GROUPS, and axes are only editable on a reproduction. A conversion needs a maintainer-agreed route, such as a source-record correction plus a new mapping. Ask before designing it.

record_exclusion.route: admin row in transform_exclusions, keyed by doi_r or url_r
record_exclusion.note: Exclusions apply to the whole replication key. Check that the key has no other row that should stay, then expect the published record to retire rather than vanish.

merge_split_relink_with_duplicate.note: Duplicate rulings and manual records are separate workflows in flora-validation; none of these belongs in a scalar batch.

preconditions: Fetch the record through GET /api/admin/flora/{id} and read its version.
Require the ledger's current values to equal the record's values for every field in the bundle; on any difference, stop that bundle and rebuild the ledger.
Send the version with the PATCH; a stale version returns 409 and that bundle stops.
Apply every field of a bundle in one request. A set stops at its first unexplained failure.
audit_log: flora_record_changes is append-only and records who, when, before and after, plus a note per field. Each note cites the ledger field id and the ledger hash.
dry_run: Build application_plan_dryrun.json, then run it against a disposable database (the flora-validation README warns that importing app.py can start jobs against the configured database) and diff the exported CSV: only the planned fields and derived columns may change.
regression_checks: row and id counts unchanged except planned exclusions
the ledger rebuilt against the new export shows every applied field as already_equal
rollback: POST /api/admin/flora/{id}/restore with the change_id recorded before the batch (0 returns to the derived value). Corrections are overlays, so source records are untouched.
authorization: Nothing here has been run. It needs an explicit user decision on the concrete rule and set, and admin access to flora-validation.
